subject.title: [Enhancement] High I/O Overhead from Synchronous Permission Hardening on State DB Commit Hot Path

question: Should OpenClaw remove unconditional post-write permission checks, and which database lifecycle event must guarantee private modes for sidecars created after startup?
rationale: The repeated work is real, but it protects credentials-adjacent files and the report does not quantify its cost; selecting a safe skip, cache, or deferred lifecycle requires owner judgment.

options.title: Benchmark lifecycle-aware deduplication
options.body: Require before-and-after measurements, then skip redundant checks only with explicit coverage for main, WAL, SHM, and rollback-journal creation and recreation.

options.title: Retain current hardening
options.body: Keep unconditional post-write checks until measured impact demonstrates that added lifecycle state is justified.

options.title: Unify SQLite permission policy
options.body: Design this together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102912 while keeping performance deduplication separate from chmod error-tolerance decisions.

recommendation.title: Benchmark lifecycle-aware deduplication
recommendation.body: Require before-and-after measurements, then skip redundant checks only with explicit coverage for main, WAL, SHM, and rollback-journal creation and recreation.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent permission helper, sidecar coverage, and state/WAL lifecycle history make this person the strongest available owner for the security-lifecycle decision.
